question: When an exact fraction rho in {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4} of training labels is replaced by a different class chosen uniformly at random, does gradient boosting with log-loss and early stopping (scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingClassifier) lose a larger share of its clean-test accuracy above the majority-class rate than a random forest (scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier), and how do both compare with L2-regularized logistic regression, on four tabular classification datasets retrieved through scikit-learn's loaders (breast_cancer, bundled; credit-g and adult via fetch_openml; covtype via fetch_covtype), each capped at a stratified sample of at most 5,000 rows, when every method gets the same tuning budget on noisy validation labels?
hypotheses: H1 (main): On each dataset, gradient boosting loses a larger share of its headroom than the random forest between rho=0 and rho=0.4. Measure, per method and dataset: the relative drop r = (A(0) - A(0.4)) / (A(0) - m), where A(rho) is clean-test accuracy averaged over the 10 seeds and m is the majority-class share of each seed's test split, averaged over the same seeds. r is the share of the method's clean-data accuracy above the majority rate that is lost at rho=0.4; two methods that both fall to the majority rate both score r = 1. Intervals: paired bootstrap over seeds (10,000 resamples, resampling the 10 seeds jointly for both methods and recomputing each r from the resampled means), 95% percentile interval of the difference. Smallest meaningful difference: 0.05 in r AND at least 1 accuracy point in the absolute drops. Exclusion (decided only from rho=0 accuracy, before any noisy condition is examined, and separately for each hypothesis): a dataset is 'uninformative' for a comparison if any method in it has A(0) - m below 5 accuracy points; a dataset is excluded whole, never a seed. Per dataset, with D = r_GBDT - r_RF: supported if the interval lies above 0 and the smallest meaningful difference is met; contradicted if the interval lies below 0 and the smallest meaningful difference is met in the other direction; 'no meaningful difference' if the interval lies inside (-0.05, 0.05); otherwise inconclusive. Overall, over the informative datasets for H1: supported if supported on at least 3/4 of them (and at least 2) and contradicted on none; contradicted if contradicted on at least half; otherwise inconclusive. Absolute drops, accuracy at every noise rate and m are reported next to every result.

H2: On each dataset, tuned logistic regression loses the smallest share of its headroom of the three methods between rho=0 and rho=0.4. Same measure, intervals, threshold and exclusion rule as H1 (applied to all three methods, so H2 may have fewer informative datasets than H1; both denominators are reported). Per dataset, with D1 = r_LR - r_GBDT and D2 = r_LR - r_RF: supported if both intervals lie below 0 and both meet the smallest meaningful difference; contradicted if either interval lies above 0 and meets it in that direction; 'no meaningful difference' if both intervals lie inside (-0.05, 0.05); otherwise inconclusive. Same overall count rule as H1.
contribution: A controlled comparison that, in the work we found, has not been made: log-loss gradient boosting with early stopping, random forests and logistic regression, with an equal tuning budget, an exact symmetric flip rate, clean test labels, per-dataset results that report accuracy at every noise rate and the majority-class rate next to each drop, and seed-level uncertainty. Rankings at each noise rate are reported descriptively, not tested.

design.summary: Within each of 10 seeds, each dataset (breast_cancer, credit-g, adult, covtype; stratified cap of 5,000 rows) is split 60/20/20, an exact nested fraction rho in {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4} of training and validation labels is replaced by a uniformly chosen other class, and HistGradientBoosting (one-hot input; early stopping on the noisy validation split, without rollback to the best iteration), RandomForest and L2 logistic regression are each tuned by random search over 20 configurations scored on noisy validation accuracy, then evaluated once on clean test labels. H1 and H2 are decided per dataset from the share of headroom above the majority rate lost between rho=0 and rho=0.4, computed from seed means, with paired 95% t(9) intervals over seeds whose standard error carries the Nadeau-Bengio correction on breast_cancer and credit-g, where every seed re-splits the same rows, and is uncorrected on adult and covtype, where every seed draws a fresh 5,000-row sample (the seed bootstrap is kept as a descriptive check), after an exclusion check that reads only rho=0 accuracy and is logged before any noisy cell is trained. Three ablations (GBDT without early stopping, selection on clean validation labels at rho=0.4, half budget) attribute a mechanism only when the paired interval of the change D_main - D_ablation excludes 0 and the change is at least 0.05; the plan is estimated at about 20 wall-minutes on 8 cores, with a contingency fixed in advance.
design.method:
EXPERIMENTAL PROCEDURE (fixed before any run on study data; any departure is logged and disclosed).

1. Seeds and random streams. Seeds s = 0..9. Datasets are indexed breast_cancer=0, credit_g=1, adult=2, covtype=3. For each (dataset d, seed s): ss = numpy.random.SeedSequence([20261118, d, s]); (sub, split, noise, cand, model) = ss.spawn(5), used in that order for the subsample, the split, the label flips, the random-search candidates and the models' random_state. Integers passed to scikit-learn are int(child.generate_state(1)[0]). The candidates stream is split by child.spawn(4) into one stream per method in the order lr, rf, gbdt, gbdt_noes. Within a (dataset, seed), the subsample, split, test set, preprocessing, candidate lists and model random_state are identical across all five rho, all methods and all ablations, so every comparison is paired by seed. This matches plan.json seed_definition (candidate draws count as the models' own randomness).

2. Subsample and split. If n > 5,000: sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split(X, y, train_size=5000, stratify=y, random_state=sub). Then test = 20% (train_test_split(test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=split)), and validation = 25% of the remainder (test_size=0.25, stratify, a second integer from the split stream). Sizes: breast_cancer 341/114/114, credit-g 600/200/200, adult and covtype 3000/1000/1000. Stratification uses the clean labels, before any flip. The code asserts that every class appears in every split (covtype class 4 has about 24 rows in a 5,000-row sample).

3. Noise injection (train and validation only; test labels are never changed). With K classes and the noise stream, draw in this order: perm_tr = rng.permutation(n_train), shift_tr = rng.integers(1, K, size=n_train), perm_va = rng.permutation(n_val), shift_va = rng.integers(1, K, size=n_val). At rate rho, n_flip = floor(rho*n + 0.5) for each split separately, the flipped set is the first n_flip indices of perm, and each flipped label becomes (y + shift) mod K, which is uniform over the K-1 other classes. Flip sets are therefore nested across rho and an example keeps the same wrong class at every rate. The code asserts: exactly n_flip labels differ from the clean labels in each split, no flipped label equals its clean label, and the test labels equal the clean labels. n_flipped_train and n_flipped_val are recorded per cell.

4. Preprocessing (identical for all three methods; one sklearn ColumnTransformer fitted on the training split's features only, then applied to validation and test). Numeric columns: SimpleImputer(strategy='median') then StandardScaler. Categorical columns (as typed in the Data RA's prepared table; credit-g and adult only): SimpleImputer(strategy='constant', fill_value='missing') then OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore', sparse_output=False). Preprocessing uses no labels, so it is the same at every rho. Scaling is a no-op for the trees; one-hot input means HGB gets categorical_features=None.

5. Estimators (scikit-learn 1.9.1) and search spaces. Each method gets N = 20 random-search configurations per (dataset, seed), drawn once from that method's candidate stream and reused at every rho. loguniform(a,b) = 10**Uniform(log10 a, log10 b); logint(a,b) = round(loguniform(a,b)).
 - LR: LogisticRegression(l1_ratio=0.0 [L2], solver='lbfgs', max_iter=2000, tol=1e-4), multinomial for covtype. Space: C ~ loguniform(1e-4, 1e2), which reaches strong regularization (van Rooyen et al.). The 'penalty' argument is deprecated in 1.9 and is not passed.
 - RF: RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200 [fixed, not tuned], criterion='gini', bootstrap=True, max_depth=None, n_jobs=1, random_state=model). Space: max_features ~ Uniform(0.05, 0.7) (fraction of columns), min_samples_leaf ~ logint(1, 50), max_samples ~ Uniform(0.5, 1.0).
 - GBDT: HistGradientBoostingClassifier(loss='log_loss', max_iter=1000, early_stopping=True [set explicitly; 'auto' would be off at these sizes], scoring='loss', n_iter_no_change=20, tol=1e-7, max_bins=255, categorical_features=None, random_state=model), fitted with fit(X_tr, y_tr_noisy, X_val=X_va, y_val=y_va_noisy), so early stopping monitors log-loss on the same noisy 20% validation split used for selection and no internal validation_fraction is carved from the training data. No rollback: in scikit-learn 1.9.1 fitting stops when none of the last 20 validation-loss scores improves by more than tol on the score 21 iterations earlier, and the returned model keeps every iteration it fitted, including the last 20; it is NOT truncated to the best validation iteration as XGBoost/LightGBM best-iteration early stopping would be. Descriptives report n_iter_ and the implied plateau n_iter_ - 20. Categorical features enter HGB as one-hot columns (categorical_features=None), not through its native categorical splits. Claims are about this exact configuration. Space: learning_rate ~ loguniform(0.01, 0.3), max_leaf_nodes ~ logint(4, 64), min_samples_leaf ~ logint(2, 100), l2_regularization ~ loguniform(1e-4, 10).
 - GBDT-noES (ablation A1 only): the GBDT space plus max_iter ~ logint(10, 500), with early_stopping=False and no X_val.

6. Tuning and selection. Every candidate is fitted on the noisy training labels and scored by accuracy on the noisy validation labels; the highest score wins, ties going to the earlier candidate. The budget is equal in number of configurations, and therefore in number of fits: 20 per method per cell. GBDT early stopping happens inside each of its 20 fits and is part of the method, not extra configurations; ablations A1 and A3 test whether it or the budget size drives the result. There is no refit on train+validation: the selected model is the one already fitted on the training split. It predicts the clean test split once. For ablation A3 the code also records the test accuracy of the best of the first 10 candidates (a different configuration, also evaluated once). No other test predictions are made.

7. Recorded per cell (dataset, method, variant, rho, seed): test_acc (clean labels; sklearn.metrics.accuracy_score), majority_rate m (share of the most frequent class in this seed's test split), test_acc_half (A3), val_acc_noisy and val_acc_clean of the selected model (clean validation labels are diagnostic only, never used for selection in the main runs), train_acc_noisy (fit to the noisy training labels), pred_majority_share (share of test predictions equal to the test majority class), the selected hyperparameters, GBDT n_iter_, n_train/n_val/n_test, K, n_flipped_train, n_flipped_val. Fit seconds are written to a separate timing file, not to the metrics, because they do not reproduce.

8. Execution. joblib with 8 worker processes over cells; threadpoolctl limits each worker to one BLAS/OpenMP thread. Results do not depend on the number of workers because every cell draws all its randomness from its own SeedSequence.

STATISTICS (code/analyze.py; per dataset, never pooled). J = 10 seeds; n_tr and n_te are the dataset's training and test sizes (341/114, 600/200, 3000/1000, 3000/1000).
 - A(rho) = mean over seeds of test_acc; m = mean over seeds of the test majority rate; SD with ddof=1.
 - r = (A(0) - A(0.4)) / (A(0) - m) from seed means; drop = A(0) - A(0.4); headroom h = A(0) - m.
 - H1: D = r_GBDT - r_RF. H2: D1 = r_LR - r_GBDT, D2 = r_LR - r_RF.
 - Decision interval (design-r1 F1, design-r2 F7; replaces the percentile bootstrap named in the hypotheses, see disclosures). Per-seed linearized values (delta method, exact first-order influence of seed s on the ratio of means): for method k, l_ks = [(a0_ks - a4_ks) - r_k (a0_ks - m_s)] / h_k, where a0_ks, a4_ks are seed s's test accuracies at rho 0 and 0.4 and m_s its test majority rate; these average to 0 over seeds. For a contrast D = r_a - r_b, u_s = l_as - l_bs and S = sample SD of u_s (ddof=1). 95% interval: D +/- t_{0.975, 9} * sqrt(c) * S, with t_{0.975, 9} = 2.262 (scipy.stats.t.ppf) and c fixed per dataset now:
   * breast_cancer and credit-g: every seed re-splits the same 569 or 1,000 rows, so the Nadeau-Bengio correction applies (nadeau2003): c = 1/J + n_te/n_tr = 0.1 + 1/3. Half-width = 1.49 S; it cannot fall below 1.13 S however many seeds are run.
   * adult and covtype: every seed draws a new stratified 5,000-row sample from 48,842 or 581,012 rows, so two seeds' training sets share about 3000^2/N = 184 rows (6%) on adult and 15 rows (0.5%) on covtype, and their test sets about 20 and 2 rows. The seed estimates are therefore close to independent and the plain paired interval is used: c = 1/J = 0.1. Half-width = 0.72 S. The small residual overlap makes this interval slightly narrow on adult; it is not corrected, and this is stated in the paper.
   Reachability: 'no meaningful difference' needs the whole interval inside (-0.05, 0.05), i.e. S < 0.034 on breast_cancer and credit-g and S < 0.070 on adult and covtype even at D = 0. S is the per-seed SD of the difference in headroom shares, roughly the per-seed SD of the paired drop difference divided by the headroom. Under assumed values (not study data: binomial test-set noise, headrooms of about 33, 5, 10 and 25 points), it is realistically reachable only on covtype, marginal on adult, and not reachable on breast_cancer or credit-g, where an 'inconclusive' outcome reflects the precision the design can deliver and is never evidence that the methods behave alike. The analysis reports S and the half-width next to every D so each result can be read against its resolution.
 - Unstable denominator: for each compared method, the 95% interval of h_k (same dataset-specific formula, per-seed values a0_ks - m_s) is computed. If its lower bound is below 0.01 for any compared method, that comparison on that dataset is reported as 'inconclusive (unstable denominator)' whatever the interval of D says. The same rule is applied to each ablation's own rho=0 headroom (design-r2 F9): A1 uses GBDT-noES's rho=0 accuracies; A3 uses the half-budget rho=0 accuracies of every method; A2 shares the main rho=0 accuracies. When it fails, Delta for that contrast is reported as 'inconclusive (unstable denominator)'.
 - Descriptive check only (never decides an outcome): the paired seed bootstrap, one index matrix of shape (10,000, 10) from numpy.random.default_rng(20261119).integers(0, 10, ...), shared by every dataset, method and contrast; r and D recomputed from resampled means; 2.5/97.5 percentiles reported next to the decision interval.
 - Smallest meaningful difference, read on point estimates: |D| >= 0.05 AND the difference in absolute drops (e.g. drop_GBDT - drop_RF) is at least 0.01 (1 accuracy point) in the same direction.
 - Per-dataset outcome, evaluated in this order: supported, contradicted, no meaningful difference (corrected interval inside (-0.05, 0.05); for H2 both intervals), inconclusive. Definitions as in plan.json hypotheses, with the corrected interval in place of the bootstrap interval. Reporting words: 'no meaningful difference' is the brief's 'no difference'; 'inconclusive' is written 'no detectable difference (inconclusive)', never 'no difference' and never a difference.
 - Overall per hypothesis, over its n informative datasets: supported if supported on >= max(2, ceil(0.75 n)) and contradicted on none; contradicted if contradicted on >= n/2 (n >= 1); otherwise inconclusive; 'not testable' if n = 0.
 - Ablation attribution (design-r1 F2). For each ablation and contrast, Delta = D_main - D_abl (and Delta1, Delta2 for H2), computed from the same seeds: per-seed values u_main,s - u_abl,s and the dataset's t(9) interval as above (Nadeau-Bengio corrected on breast_cancer and credit-g, plain on adult and covtype). A1: D_abl = r_GBDT-noES - r_RF (RF cells shared with main). A2: D_abl uses each method's clean-validation-selected accuracy at rho=0.4 and the main rho=0 accuracy (clean and noisy validation labels coincide at rho=0). A3: D_abl uses test_acc_half at both rates. A mechanism is attributed (A1: early stopping; A2: noisy model selection; A3: budget size) only when the Delta interval excludes 0 AND |Delta| >= 0.05. Otherwise the paper reports the ablation's D, interval and Delta descriptively and says the ablation did not distinguish the explanations. Outcome categories of an ablation are never compared with the main categories as evidence.
 - Exclusion (code/exclusion.py, run exclusion-check): reads only the rho=0 cell file. For H1 a dataset is uninformative if A(0) - m < 0.05 for GBDT or RF; for H2, if it is below 0.05 for any of the three. It writes results/exclusion.json, which code/analyze.py reads and never recomputes. The ablations use the main exclusion sets unchanged; their own denominators are checked by the unstable-denominator rule.
 - Rankings at each rho order the three methods by A(rho) and are descriptive only. Ties are not resolved by test; a ranking difference is labelled 'within noise' when the dataset's 95% paired t(9) interval for the accuracy gap (with the same Nadeau-Bengio correction as the decision intervals on breast_cancer and credit-g, uncorrected on adult and covtype) contains 0 (design-r3 F11).

COMPUTE AND CONTINGENCY (design-r1 F5). Hardware: the PI's laptop, Apple M3, 8 CPU cores (4 performance + 4 efficiency), 8 joblib workers; this is the reading of 'laptop CPU' (disclosed). Estimate from timing-synthetic: about 134 CPU-minutes, about 20 wall-minutes for every planned run; timing-covtype-stress (harder synthetic covtype) gave cheaper covtype GBDT cells (mean 67 iterations, 20 s per cell against 36 s), but a harder problem stops earlier, so that run does not bound the costly case, a learnable problem on which validation loss keeps improving for hundreds of iterations at low learning rates. The all-fits-to-1000-iterations bound is about 530 CPU-minutes for covtype GBDT alone. The W0-triggered contingency below, not the stress run, guards this cost: rho=0 covtype GBDT cells run in main-rho0. Contingency, fixed now and triggered only by the wall time W0 of main-rho0 (a time, which carries no information about noise effects): projected total = 7 x W0 (rho=0 is about 1/7 of the fit cost in timing-synthetic). If the projection exceeds 45 minutes, drop ablation A1 (abl-noes); if it still exceeds 45 minutes without A1 (6.1 x W0), drop A2 (abl-cleanval) too. A3 needs no fits and is always run. Seeds, noise rates, N = 20, datasets and methods are never reduced. If main alone overruns 60 minutes, it is run in full and the overrun is reported as a deviation. Any contingency taken is logged with crew.py log and disclosed. The Replicator's clean rerun is a second pass of the same runs and is expected to take the same time.
design.data:
Four datasets, each pinned by the Data RA in data/manifest.json (origin, OpenML data_id and version where applicable, license, sha256, retrieval date) before any analysis run; the design names the dataset, not the file, and no run may use an unpinned version.
 - breast_cancer: sklearn.datasets.load_breast_cancer (bundled with scikit-learn 1.9.1). 569 rows, 30 numeric features, 2 classes (63/37). No cap applies; split 341/114/114.
 - credit-g: fetch_openml (German credit; data_id and version pinned by the Data RA). 1,000 rows, 7 numeric + 13 categorical features (about 61 columns after one-hot), 2 classes (70/30). Split 600/200/200.
 - adult: fetch_openml (data_id and version pinned; OpenML has several 'adult' entries). About 48,842 rows, 6 numeric + 8 categorical features with missing values in workclass, occupation and native-country (about 108 columns after one-hot), 2 classes (about 76/24). Stratified 5,000-row sample per seed; split 3000/1000/1000. fnlwgt is kept as a feature, as the loader provides it; no row is dropped for missing values (they are imputed as a 'missing' category). The 52 exact duplicate rows (data/CODEBOOK.md) are kept: they are in the pinned reference data (OpenML data_id 1590 version 2, as in OpenML-CC18) and in the UCI data, and removing them would make our adult differ from the data other studies used; in a 5,000-row sample the expected number of duplicated pairs is about 52 x (5000/48842)^2 = 0.5, and a pair lands in train and test in fewer than 0.15 per seed, the same for every method, so the effect on any comparison is negligible.
 - covtype: sklearn.datasets.fetch_covtype (pinned by hash). 581,012 rows, 54 features (10 numeric, 44 binary indicators kept as numeric), 7 classes (largest about 48.8%; class 4 about 0.5%). Stratified 5,000-row sample per seed; split 3000/1000/1000.
Unit of observation: one row (one example). Target: the dataset's own label, encoded to integers 0..K-1 by the Data RA's prepare step. Features: all columns the loader provides except the target; no feature selection. The only sample restriction is the 5,000-row stratified cap. Label noise is synthetic and is added by the experiment code, never by the data-prep step. Unit of analysis for the hypotheses: the (dataset, method, rho, seed) cell, aggregated to seed means per dataset.
analysis_plan: timing-synthetic (data-prep, designer; DONE 2026-11-18): code/timing_synthetic.py times the planned per-cell procedure on make_classification data with the four post-cap shapes (64 cells, 20 configurations, 8 workers). It reads no study data. Purpose: fix the tuning budget N before any study run. Result: about 134 CPU-minutes and 19 wall-minutes for the whole plan below at N=20, so N=20 is fixed.

timing-covtype-stress (data-prep, designer; DONE 2026-11-18): code/timing_covtype_stress.py reruns the covtype GBDT cells on a harder synthetic set (20 informative columns, 4 clusters per class, class_sep 0.8) and times one boosting iteration. It reads no study data. Purpose: design-r1 F5's concern about covtype GBDT cost. Result: mean 67 iterations and about 20 s per cell; a harder problem stops earlier, so this does not bound the costly case (design-r2 F8); the per-iteration worst-case bound is in its timing.json, and the main-rho0 contingency guards the cost.

data prep (data-prep, data-ra): fetch and pin the four datasets in data/manifest.json and write a prepared table per dataset (typed features, integer target). Purpose: fixed, versioned inputs. Must be finished before main-rho0.

code review (reviewer, target 'code'): check code/experiment.py, code/exclusion.py and code/analyze.py against design.method before any analysis run, in particular which labels selection and early stopping see, the flip assertions, the shared candidate lists and the bootstrap. Purpose: catch leakage and deviations before results exist.

main-rho0 (analysis, experimenter): code/experiment.py --rhos 0 --variant main: 4 datasets x 3 methods x 10 seeds = 120 cells, 20 configurations each. Output results/cells_rho0.csv; ledger metrics are A(0) mean and SD and m per (dataset, method). Purpose: clean-data baseline and the input to the exclusion check. Estimate: about 3 wall-minutes. Its wall time W0 sets the compute contingency in design.method (projected total 7 x W0; above 45 minutes drop A1, then A2).

exclusion-check (analysis, experimenter): code/exclusion.py reads only results/cells_rho0.csv and writes results/exclusion.json (headroom A(0) - m per method and dataset; informative datasets for H1 and for H2). It must appear in the ledger before main-noisy starts. Purpose: decide exclusion from clean accuracy alone, as hypotheses H1/H2 require.

main-noisy (analysis, experimenter): code/experiment.py --rhos 0.1 0.2 0.3 0.4 --variant main: 480 cells. Output results/cells_noisy.csv; ledger metrics are A(rho) mean and SD per (dataset, method, rho). Purpose: the main experiment. Estimate: about 11 wall-minutes.

h-tests (analysis, experimenter): code/analyze.py --test main reads both cell files and results/exclusion.json and computes, per dataset, A(0), A(0.4), m, h, drop and r per method, D (H1), D1 and D2 (H2), their paired t(9) 95% intervals (the decision intervals: Nadeau-Bengio corrected on breast_cancer and credit-g, plain on adult and covtype), S and the half-width, the headroom-stability check, the descriptive seed-bootstrap percentile intervals, the per-dataset outcomes and the overall verdicts with their denominators. Purpose: decide H1 and H2 with the pre-registered rules.

descriptives (analysis, experimenter): code/analyze.py --describe writes the accuracy table (mean and SD over 10 seeds) at every rho for every dataset and method, m, absolute drops, rankings at each rho with the 'within noise' label, the selected hyperparameters per rho (median and IQR of LR C, RF min_samples_leaf and max_features, GBDT learning_rate and n_iter_), noisy and clean validation accuracy of the selected models, train_acc_noisy, pred_majority_share, and checks that n_flipped equals floor(rho*n + 0.5) in every cell. Purpose: everything the hypotheses say must be reported next to each result, plus the tuned C at each rate (notes.md, design-stage note 4).

abl-noes (analysis, experimenter): A1. code/experiment.py --rhos 0 0.4 --variant gbdt_noes: GBDT without early stopping, max_iter in the search, same 20-configuration budget, 80 cells; then code/analyze.py --test noes computes D_abl = r_GBDT-noES - r_RF and Delta = D_main - D_abl with the dataset's paired t(9) interval. The unstable-denominator rule is applied to GBDT-noES's own rho=0 headroom. Purpose: early stopping on noisy labels is credited with the H1 result only if the Delta interval excludes 0 and |Delta| >= 0.05 (Eisenbuerger et al. found early stopping matters); otherwise reported descriptively. First to be dropped under the compute contingency. Estimate: about 2.5 wall-minutes.

abl-cleanval (analysis, experimenter): A2. code/experiment.py --rhos 0.4 --variant cleanval: all three methods at rho=0.4 with noisy training labels but candidates scored, and GBDT early-stopped, on the CLEAN validation labels; the same candidate lists. 120 cells. rho=0 needs no rerun, because clean and noisy validation labels coincide there. code/analyze.py --test cleanval computes D_abl, D1_abl, D2_abl and Delta, Delta1, Delta2 with the dataset's paired t(9) intervals. Purpose: noisy model selection is credited with an H1 or H2 result only if the Delta interval excludes 0 and |Delta| >= 0.05; otherwise reported descriptively. Second to be dropped under the compute contingency. Estimate: about 3 wall-minutes.

abl-budget (analysis, experimenter): A3. code/analyze.py --test half recomputes D, D1, D2 from test_acc_half (best of the first 10 of the same 20 candidates; recorded in the main runs; no new fits) and Delta = D_main - D_half with the dataset's paired t(9) intervals. The unstable-denominator rule is applied to the half-budget rho=0 headroom. Purpose: budget size is credited only if a Delta interval excludes 0 and |Delta| >= 0.05, in particular whether the 1-dimensional LR space gains more from 20 configurations than the 3- and 4-dimensional tree spaces. Always run (no fits).

figures (analysis, figures-ra): accuracy against rho per dataset (mean +/- SD over seeds, one line per method, a horizontal line at m) and a forest plot of D, D1, D2 with their decision intervals (bootstrap intervals as a lighter second mark) for main and ablations, built only from the result files of the runs above.

rerun (replicator): crew.py rerun in an environment built only from code/requirements.txt; every metric must reproduce at rtol 1e-6. Fit times are kept out of the metrics, so they cannot break the comparison.
threats: Unequal effective tuning: LR searches one dimension and the trees three or four, and GBDT early stopping on the noisy validation split adds a free choice of the number of iterations that RF and LR do not get. Equal configuration counts do not guarantee equal tuning quality. Addressed by A1 (GBDT without early stopping) and A3 (half budget), each judged by the paired t(9) interval of Delta = D_main - D_ablation, and by reporting the selected hyperparameters at every rho.

The ordering may come from model selection on noisy validation labels rather than from the learners: a 40% noisy validation split of 200 rows is a weak selector. Addressed by A2 (selection and early stopping on clean validation labels at rho=0.4), judged by the paired t(9) interval of Delta, and by reporting clean versus noisy validation accuracy of the selected models.

Ratio instability (question-review F16): r divides by the headroom A(0) - m, which is about 5 points on credit-g. Addressed by computing r from seed means (never per seed), by the 5-point exclusion read from rho=0 only and logged before any noisy cell is trained (exclusion-check precedes main-noisy in the ledger), by the headroom-stability rule (the 95% interval of h, for main and ablation denominators, must stay above 1 point, else 'inconclusive (unstable denominator)'), and by reporting absolute drops next to r.

Re-split variance on fixed rows and limited resolution (design-r1 F1, design-r2 F7): on breast_cancer and credit-g every seed re-splits the same 569 or 1,000 rows, so the spread across seeds understates the variance relevant to a claim about the dataset, and a percentile bootstrap over 10 seeds under-covers (about 90% at nominal 95%). Addressed by the Nadeau-Bengio corrected t(9) interval on those two datasets (half-width 1.49 S, never below 1.13 S at any J) and the plain paired t(9) interval on adult and covtype (half-width 0.72 S), where fresh 5,000-row samples share only about 6% and 0.5% of training rows between seeds; the bootstrap is descriptive only. The correction is approximate (it assumes a correlation n_te/n_tr between re-splits). 'No meaningful difference' is realistically reachable only on covtype (marginal on adult), so wide intervals and 'inconclusive' outcomes are expected on breast_cancer and credit-g. Such results are reported as 'no detectable difference (inconclusive)', with S and the half-width, never as 'no difference'.

Majority-class floor on credit-g (70%) and adult (about 76%): at rho=0.4 a degraded model drifts to predicting the majority class. r = 1 for any method at the floor, so both-at-floor gives D = 0; pred_majority_share is reported to show when a method has collapsed to the floor.

Leakage: preprocessing is fitted on training features only and uses no labels; test labels are never flipped and never used in selection; each selected configuration (and the half-budget selection for A3) touches the test set once. The code review checks this before any run.
Flip implementation errors (wrong count, a 'flip' to the same class, flipped test labels, K=7 handling on covtype): addressed by assertions in the code and by the n_flipped check in descriptives.

Rare covtype classes: class 4 has about 24 rows per 5,000-row sample, about 5 per test split; uniform flips push extra examples into rare classes. Stratified splits are asserted to contain every class. Accuracy is dominated by classes 1 and 2, and the paper says so.

Forking paths after results: every choice above is fixed at the design gate; the exclusion file is produced before noisy cells exist; the analysis reads exclusion.json and does not recompute it. Any deviation is recorded in plan.json disclosures and in the paper.

Compute overrun on real data, where GBDT may run more iterations than on synthetic data (covtype at low learning rates): the estimate is about 20 wall-minutes against a 60-minute budget on 8 cores. A contingency triggered only by main-rho0's wall time drops A1, then A2, if the projected total exceeds 45 minutes; seeds, rates, N, datasets and methods are never reduced, and the budget is never cut after outcomes exist. An overrun of the main runs themselves is reported as a deviation.

Scope: four datasets, at most 3,000 training rows, scikit-learn 1.9.1 implementations, symmetric noise, accuracy. The GBDT arm is HistGradientBoosting on one-hot-encoded categoricals with early stopping that keeps the 20 post-plateau iterations (no rollback to the best iteration), which differs from XGBoost/LightGBM best-iteration early stopping and from native categorical handling. Claims are limited to these datasets, sizes and this configuration, and say nothing about full-size covtype or adult, other GBDT libraries or stopping rules, or class-dependent noise.
Dataset version drift (several OpenML 'adult' entries): data_id, version and sha256 are pinned in data/manifest.json before any analysis run, and crew.py validate checks the hashes.

design.summary: Design passed review in round 3; two minor findings answered by the PI afterwards.
design.note: Approved in chat on 2026-11-18 after reading the Reviewer's verdict, kill argument and disclosures. The analysis plan is now fixed.

disclosures: 2026-11-18: During the round-1 review of the question, the Reviewer ran an untuned 5-seed pilot of the three methods on iris, wine and digits outside the workspace. Its results informed the revised question (per-dataset reporting, decision rules). None of those three datasets is in the study.

2026-11-18: Dataset choice. The seed brief asks for datasets that ship with scikit-learn. Its bundled classification sets are iris, wine, digits and breast_cancer; the first three were used in the Reviewer's pilot and digits is image data, so only breast_cancer remains. The PI therefore added three tabular datasets retrieved through scikit-learn loaders: adult and covtype, because prior label-noise studies used them (Le Baher et al.; Eisenbuerger et al.), and credit-g, a small imbalanced dataset with no prior label-noise study that we found. This departs from the brief. Exact OpenML data_id, version and file hash are pinned in data/manifest.json before any run.

2026-11-18 (design stage, before any run on study data): Decision interval changed. The approved hypotheses name a 95% percentile interval from a paired bootstrap over the 10 seeds. After design reviews design-r1 F1 and design-r2 F7 the design replaces it with a paired t(9) interval over seeds: on breast_cancer and credit-g, where every seed re-splits the same rows, its standard error carries the Nadeau-Bengio (2003) correction (variance factor 1/J + n_test/n_train); on adult and covtype, where every seed draws a fresh 5,000-row sample (about 6% and 0.5% training-row overlap between seeds), it is uncorrected. The bootstrap, which under-covers with 10 seeds, is kept as a descriptive check. Thresholds, exclusion and count rules are unchanged. With these intervals 'no meaningful difference' is realistically reachable only on covtype and perhaps adult.

2026-11-18: Departure from seed requirement 2 ('Noise is injected into training labels only; test labels stay clean'). Test labels stay clean, but the validation labels used for tuning and early stopping are flipped at the same rate as the training labels, because they are part of the labelled data a practitioner has (question-review ruling on F4). Ablation A2 gives the clean-validation variant at rho=0.4.

2026-11-18: Interpretation of seed requirement 4 ('differences inside the noise are reported as no difference'). A difference whose interval includes 0 is never reported as a difference. It is reported as 'no meaningful difference', which is this study's 'no difference', when the whole corrected 95% interval lies inside (-0.05, 0.05) on the headroom-share scale, and otherwise as 'no detectable difference (inconclusive)', because a wide interval does not show that the methods behave alike.

2026-11-18: 'Laptop CPU' is read as the PI's laptop, an Apple M3 with 8 cores (4 performance + 4 efficiency), with 8 parallel worker processes. The design estimates about 134 CPU-minutes (about 20 wall-minutes); on a machine with fewer than about 3 cores the study would not fit the one-hour budget.
seed_definition: A seed redraws, in this order: the stratified subsample (where a dataset exceeds 5,000 rows), the 60/20/20 train/validation/test split, the set of training and validation labels that are flipped and their new classes, and the models' own randomness. Test labels are never flipped.
